Processing_Method: Download WDPA (World Database of Protected Areas) for Nigeria. Filter: STATUS = Designated or Inscribed (not Proposed). Clip to study area + 10km buffer. Retain WDPA attributes: WDPAID; NAME; DESIG; IUCN_CAT; STATUS; STATUS_YR; GOV_TYPE; OWN_TYPE; REP_AREA. Add: overlap with G01 states and G02 LGAs via spatial join.
Key_QC_Rules: Record WDPA download date — updated monthly. Verify geometry validity. Cross-check: total protected area per state against IUCN Nigeria statistics (within 5% tolerance). IUCN category I–IV are strictly protected; V–VI allow sustainable use — document category in outputs. Unverified/proposed PAs must be excluded from analysis unless explicitly noted."

Processing_Method: Three-component model: (1) Land cover naturalness score — assign each G15 class a naturalness weight (HAB01=10; HAB02=10; HAB03=7; HAB04=9; HAB05=10; HAB06=4; HAB07=2; HAB08=3; HAB09=0; HAB10=0) / 10 × 100. (2) Forest loss penalty — subtract proportion of forest lost (G53) within 1km radius. (3) Landscape fragmentation — compute patch density using moving window (landscape metrics). Normalise and combine: Naturalness 50% + Forest loss 30% + Fragmentation 20%.
Key_QC_Rules: Naturalness weights must be formally approved and stored in LKP_HabitatTypes.csv (add Naturalness_Score column). Fragmentation metric (patch density or effective mesh size) must be documented with window size. Cross-validate: G59 protected area cells should have higher G60 scores than unprotected cells of same habitat type. Agricultural areas (HAB06/07) should always score lower than natural habitats.

Processing_Method: For each major river segment in G05: extract a 200m buffer (both banks). Assess: (1) Forest cover proportion within buffer from G52. (2) Forest loss proportion from G53 within buffer. (3) Continuity — proportion of buffer with unbroken natural vegetation. Score each segment 0–100: high score = intact riparian corridor. Aggregate to reach level. Mark critical corridors: segments with < 20% natural cover.
Key_QC_Rules: 200m riparian buffer must be documented in BUFFER_RULES.csv — add BUF010. Cross-check: river segments near active erosion sites (G26) should have lower G61 scores. Hydropower facility reaches (G07 ±2km) must be explicitly assessed — reservoir impoundment creates different riparian context. Flag segments with < 20% natural cover as CRITICAL_RIPARIAN_LOSS.

Processing_Method: Assign ecosystem service value weights to each habitat type (see LKP_HabitatTypes.csv). Services: water regulation; carbon storage; food provisioning; biodiversity; erosion control; flood attenuation; pollination. Compute composite ecosystem service score per pixel based on G60 habitat integrity × service weight for dominant service. Aggregate to community-level polygon.
Key_QC_Rules: Ecosystem service weights must be from a published and approved source (e.g. TEEB / InVEST / SEEA values adapted for West Africa). Document all weights and sources in ECOSYSTEM_SERVICES_METHODOLOGY.md. Do not assign monetary values without explicit approval — use relative scores only at baseline. G59 protected areas add a conservation multiplier of 1.2 to service scores within their boundaries.

Processing_Method: Community-level biodiversity loss score (BL_Score 0–100) combining: (1) Habitat integrity deficit — 100 minus mean G60 score within 5km of community (higher deficit = higher loss). (2) Deforestation rate — normalised G53 annual loss rate within community watershed. (3) Protected area gap — proportion of community area NOT covered by G59. (4) Riparian condition — mean G61 score within 5km inverted (lower condition = higher loss). Weights: Habitat 35% + Deforestation 30% + PA gap 20% + Riparian 15%.
Key_QC_Rules: Weights must be approved before computation (add to HAZARD_MODEL_DECISIONS.csv — HMD09). Cross-check: communities adjacent to G59 protected areas should have lower BL_Score. Communities with high G53 deforestation rate should have high BL_Score. Field biodiversity observations (DB09) used to validate: communities with high diversity counts should have low BL_Score.
